title: Humanizer is a free Claude skill that deletes every AI tell
description:
Humanizer is a free, open-source Claude skill that strips the AI tells out of your writing, and you install it with a single prompt.

Every large language model — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini — writes with the same fingerprint: the em dash pile-up, the three-item list every single time, the tidy closing paragraph that restates what you just read. Readers clock those tells from a mile away, and the moment they do, they stop trusting the text.

Humanizer is one markdown file that writes all of those tells down in one place, built off Wikipedia's own "Signs of AI writing" guide rather than somebody's guesses. You drop it into Claude Code as a skill, and your AI stops reaching for the patterns that give it away.

The part that separates it from every other humanizer tool: it passes over your text twice. Once to rewrite the tells out, then a second time to check it did not invent anything that was not in the original. Most tools in this category quietly change your facts to make the prose flow — Humanizer leaves the meaning exactly as written and only removes the giveaways.

Free, MIT-licensed, and it works with Claude Code today.

Get the repo: https://github.com/blader/humanizer

#humanizer #aiwriting #claudecode #github #aislop
